answer: A stake-bonded reputation graph makes each identity expensive: to join, an agent locks a deposit and links its work history to a single vertex in a shared trust graph, so a fake swarm must fund every vertex separately. Honest agents earn opal-graded endorsements from peers they served, while a Sybil cluster that only vouches for itself stays visibly isolated and earns nothing. Attackers can still buy in, but each fake identity costs real stake plus time, like bees spending nectar to build a comb, so flooding the economy stops paying.
